record.paper_title: Open Problems in Universal Induction & Intelligence
record.original_question: Can the 'prediction with expert advice' paradigm be extended from passive prediction and active learning to the full reinforcement-learning setting in a way that produces a viable alternative or dual to AIXI, or does the failure of such an extension instead show that AIXI occupies a distinguished position?

evidence.quote: a) Action with expert advice. Expected performance bounds for predictions based on Solomonoff’s prior exist. Inspired by Solomonoff induction, a dual, currently very popular approach, is “prediction with expert advice” (PEA) [LW89, Vov92, CBL06]. ... PEA has been generalized to active learning [PH05b, CBL06], but the full reinforcement learning case is still open [PH06b]. If successful, it could result in a model dual to AIXI, but I expect the answer to be negative, which on the positive side would show the distinguishedness of AIXI.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. In the prediction-with-expert-advice (PEA) framework, a learner observes, at each round t = 1, 2, ..., the predictions of a (finite or countable) class E of experts, issues its own prediction, and then receives an outcome and incurs a bounded loss. Classical results provide regret bounds of the form L_T(learner) − inf_{e ∈ E} L_T(e) = o(T) (e.g., O(√(T log |E|))), so that the learner competes with the best expert in hindsight without any probabilistic assumption on the outcome sequence. PEA has been generalized to the active-learning setting, where the learner additionally chooses queries that influence which information is revealed but not the outcomes themselves.

Reinforcement-learning setting. Consider a general (history-based, possibly non-Markovian) reinforcement-learning interaction between an agent and an unknown environment: at each time t the agent selects an action a_t ∈ A, the environment returns an observation o_t ∈ O and a bounded reward r_t ∈ [0, 1], where the environment is an arbitrary computable (or merely measurable) function from interaction histories to distributions over (o_t, r_t). Let Π be a given countable class of "expert" policies π : (A × O × R)^* → A. The agent's cumulative reward up to horizon T is V_T(agent) = Σ_{t=1}^T r_t.

Question. Does there exist an agent (a single policy, possibly randomized and history-dependent) that, for every environment in a sufficiently rich class (e.g., the class of all lower-semicomputable environments, or all stochastic environments) and for every countable expert class Π, achieves a sublinear regret guarantee of the form

   sup_{π ∈ Π} E[V_T(π)] − E[V_T(agent)] = o(T) as T → ∞,

where the expectations are taken in the true environment with the agent (resp. expert π) controlling the actions? Equivalently, can the PEA paradigm be lifted from passive prediction and active learning to the full reinforcement-learning case so as to yield a universal "experts-style" agent dual to AIXI? Or, alternatively, prove an impossibility result showing that no such agent exists for any sufficiently expressive expert class, thereby exhibiting a distinguished status for the Bayes-optimal AIXI construction.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of extending prediction-with-expert-advice to the full reinforcement-learning setting (with a regret guarantee against an arbitrary policy class in arbitrary environments) is widely cited as an open problem in the universal-AI literature. The PEA paradigm has been extended to active learning, but no general PEA-style agent for the full RL case dual to AIXI has been established, and no definitive impossibility theorem singling out AIXI has been proved.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Universal Induction & Intelligence
status_evidence.snippet: PEA has been generalized to active learning, but the full reinforcement learning case is still open. If successful, it could result in a model dual to AIXI.
status_evidence.claim: States the extension of PEA to full RL is open.

status_evidence.title: What is AIXI? - Jan Leike
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of AIXI and universal RL, with PEA-style results restricted to prediction/active settings.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys of universal RL do not report a general PEA-to-RL extension.
